answer: One defence is to make every identity earn its standing through a long, verifiable voyage of useful work rather than a one-time registration. An agent begins with a narrow thread of trust: it can only take small, low-value jobs, and each completed job adds a marble of reputation that is publicly recorded and hard to transfer. Creating a thousand fake identities therefore means funding a thousand slow voyages, each paid for in real compute and real time, while a single honest agent compounds its thread into genuine standing. Sybil attackers face a cost that scales with every identity they mint.
